dynamic_query_widths.interpretation: a first-pass mean near the second-pass mean and a modest max/p50 ratio mean dynamic widths do not cause pathological JIT or scheduling; large ratios would be reported as a measured problem before any bucketing change

lifecycle.plateau_rule: slope < 1 MiB per cycle from the second reading to the last

pool.family: KQRvK, white to move, >= 16 legal moves

qualification_gate_details.detail: every non-STOP parameter tensor has a finite non-zero gradient
qualification_gate_details.name: gradient_coverage_non_stop

qualification_gate_details.detail: STOP head gradient exactly zero while masked
qualification_gate_details.name: stop_head_gradient_exactly_zero

resident_model_vram.rule: plateau iff VRAM grows by at most 64 MiB (two allocator pages) from the second sample to the last

sustained_load.note: nvidia-smi samples every 500 ms; utilization is the fraction of the sample window in which any kernel ran, so it overstates how full the device is.

synchronisation_policy: timing_sync = true: the device is synchronised (Backend::sync) before every section clock read, so GPU section times are completion times; health checks add host reads (reported separately as the without_health_checks columns); the selector result is read to the host every round because the exact query is a CPU operation
